source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project (IFAD-funded) - "Climate Resilient Banana Growing Technique" (ផលិតកម្មដំណាំចេកដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ), November 2018
text:
Each banana clump naturally produces multiple side suckers as it grows, but letting all of them develop crowds the clump and reduces bunch size on every stem. The booklet recommends keeping only one well-placed follow-on sucker per fruiting stem at a time, removing the rest, so that as the main stem is harvested a single strong successor is already established to continue the clump's production cycle.

This staggered one-generation-at-a-time approach keeps the clump productive continuously rather than all stems maturing and being harvested at once, giving farmers a steadier flow of bunches over time from the same planted area.
